CONFIRMED in source. scripts/orch-row-prose-ceiling-check.mjs STRUCTURAL_FIELDS (line 128) contains secondary_claimed_at/secondary_claimed_by (lines 154-155, added 08-15 for exactly this reason) and ZERO occurrences of po_manual_dispatch (grep count 0). So the four po_manual_dispatch_* stamp fields count as prose against the 12000B ceiling, and the sweep's rank-1 candidate is prose-frozen at 34589B -> orch-apply hard-aborts. Because flag_reentrant() only excludes freshly-stamped rows, that row holds rank 1 permanently and the other 105 candidates never get a turn. Second family to hit the identical gap; the fix is a field-list addition, not a per-row prose trim.

CONFIRMED at bctcImageFetchDegradedSignalWriter.ts:67 - `return occurrenceCountIncludingThisPush === threshold;` (strict ===, threshold default 2). So the signal fires on exactly the 2nd occurrence and nothing amends the row when a 3rd arrives; unit-0006 was refined 10s after the signal's own ts and never made it in. Line 89 templates the '<=0.6 confidence' string unconditionally without ever reading a confidence. Live values are 0.75/0.65/0.70 - none at or below 0.6. The consequence po identified is the load-bearing one: the 0.6 cap is asserted in three places and enforced nowhere, so any consumer filtering confidence <= 0.6 returns ZERO rows for a report with three degraded units. Minted as backlog.509 P1 - the consumer-blindness argument arguably makes it P0.

po held back 27 of 82 inbox envelopes - every type with no Pipeline-A routing row - and did NOT run guard-signal-type-coverage.sh (correct: that script writes live orch-state.json via ORCH_APPLY_LIVE_FILE_OVERRIDE and --check is a no-op alias; there is no safe invocation). It hand-replayed the two extractors instead. The unrouted set grew 2 -> 9 in 17 hours, and five of the seven new types have perfectly good Pipeline-B rows - they read unrouted only because of the deliberate per-pipeline scoping. That is a scoping artefact inflating a real gap, and it means the guard's headline count cannot be read as 'types with no routing anywhere'. Holding the envelopes back is the correct play per the inverse-mode lesson: clearing them would have turned the gap green without a single routing row being added.
